summary: The candidate-pool mechanism is deterministic and correctly placed after RRF, but its signature can collapse candidates that differ on safety-relevant catalog attributes enforced elsewhere in matching.
issues: `StructuralSignature` omits `thread_type`, `working_medium`, `body_material_grade`, and valve designation/series evidence. Two candidates differing only in one of these fields receive the same signature; the lower-RRF compatible candidate can be deferred beyond the reranker limit while an incompatible one remains. This creates a concrete false-match/regression path.

The tests verify only fields included in the signature. They do not prove that candidates differing in each enforced-but-omitted constraint remain independently eligible, so they do not fully test the stated claim of safely removing only redundant structures.
Public evaluation did not run because Qdrant was unavailable. This is infrastructure-related, not a reason to discard the implementation, but the experiment is currently unmeasured.
fix_plan: Expand the conservative redundancy definition so candidates distinguishable by any catalog-observable, constraint-enforced attribute are not collapsed; fail open where designation/grade/medium evidence cannot be normalized reliably.

Add focused diversification and hybrid tests where the only difference is thread type, working medium, material grade, and designation/series, asserting both candidates remain before the reranker budget.
Re-run public evaluation once Qdrant is available and compare quality and safety metrics with the champion before blind gating.
next_direction: Candidate diversification remains a plausible retrieval-pool experiment, but safety requires treating all constraint-relevant catalog distinctions as non-redundant; do not infer effectiveness from the current unit tests or the unavailable public evaluation.
